items.stem: A nurse gives the wrong dose because two drug vials look almost identical and are stored together. A systems approach would first focus on:

options.text: Redesigning storage and labelling to make the error hard to repeat
options.rationale: Correct: a systems view targets the conditions that allowed the error, such as look-alike storage.

options.text: Disciplining the nurse to deter future errors
options.rationale: Blaming the individual ignores the system factors and does not prevent recurrence.

options.text: Asking staff to be more careful
options.rationale: Exhortations to be careful are weak and unreliable against latent system hazards.

options.text: Removing the incident from the record
options.rationale: Hiding the event prevents learning and improvement.

items.explanation: Correct: a systems view targets the conditions that allowed the error, such as look-alike storage.

items.stem: In the Model for Improvement, what is the purpose of a PDSA cycle?

options.text: To test a change on a small scale and learn before wider rollout
options.rationale: Correct: Plan-Do-Study-Act tests a change in small, rapid cycles to learn and adapt.

options.text: To audit compliance once a year
options.rationale: PDSA is iterative testing of change, not an annual compliance audit.

options.text: To assign blame after an incident
options.rationale: PDSA is an improvement method, not an incident-blaming tool.
PDSA relies on measurement to judge whether a change is an improvement.

items.explanation: Correct: Plan-Do-Study-Act tests a change in small, rapid cycles to learn and adapt.

items.stem: Which TWO are features of a 'just culture' in patient safety? (Select TWO)

options.text: Staff are encouraged to report errors and near misses openly
options.rationale: Correct: open reporting without fear of unfair punishment is central to a just culture.

options.text: A clear, fair line is drawn for reckless behaviour
options.rationale: Correct: a just culture still holds reckless conduct accountable while supporting honest error.

options.text: No one is ever held accountable for any action
options.rationale: That is a blame-free culture; a just culture retains accountability for recklessness.

options.text: All errors are kept confidential and never analysed
options.rationale: A just culture analyses errors to learn, rather than hiding them.

items.explanation: Correct: open reporting without fear of unfair punishment is central to a just culture.
